headline: Ofqual plans changes to A Level coursework as AI cheating fears grow
summary: England’s exams regulator says it will soon propose changes to coursework in A Level history and English, and wants invigilators trained to spot cheating devices by summer 2027.
body: Sir Ian Bauckham, Chief Regulator at Ofqual, told the Schools and Academies Show in Birmingham on 18 November that using AI to cheat in coursework “will not be tolerated”. He warned students that the penalties for serious cheating can include losing their qualifications.

Ofqual regulates qualifications in England. In a letter to exam boards the same day, it said it will soon propose changes to non-exam assessment in A Level history and the three A Level English qualifications, and may change other subjects too. Bauckham said the changes will cause as little disruption as possible to students already on courses. He also warned that AI detection will soon reach its limits.
He quoted a Teacher Tapp poll: 70% of secondary teachers don’t think unsupervised written coursework should count towards final grades, and 83% want more supervision or other controls.

Ofqual also wants exam boards to tackle wearable devices sold for cheating in exams. It expects invigilators to get consistent training to spot them in time for the summer 2027 exams, and has asked exam boards to reply before 30 November.
do_this: If your child is doing A Level coursework, ask their teacher what the school allows AI to be used for.
Remind them that serious cheating, including with AI, can cost them the whole qualification.
